| [CLAIM-306](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-306.md) | "If I can't find it, it isn't there" | The medic's "If I can't find it, it isn't there" ([CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md)) and the owner's "if I can't find it quickly enough, it may as well not be there" ([CASE-094](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-094.md)) act on a failed search as if it showed absence. One find shows presence, but absence needs a check of everything, which a deadline forbids. First filed as negation as failure on a time bound, with Reiter and Clark unread. Both readings corrected it. The two assumptions are separate. Reiter's closed-world assumption is that the database is complete about the world. Clark's negation as failure is licensed only by finite failure: "the exhaustive but unsuccessful search for a proof". A search cut off by a deadline meets neither, so the rule is stronger than both. It assumes a closed world and that the unsearched part would have failed. It is safe when the full pass finishes in time. In [CASE-085](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-085.md) the EMT knew the drug was stocked, which is exactly where Reiter shows the closed-world assumption inconsistent.
